🇪🇺 EU leaders fail to agree on 2028–2034 budget, talks pushed to December EU leaders ended their special summit in Brussels without a deal on the bloc's next seven-year budget. They also failed to agree on a new €45 billion loan for Ukraine. European Council President António Costa's compromise puts the budget at around €1.58 trillion, roughly €200 billion less than the European Commission originally proposed. It still satisfies almost no one, often for opposite reasons. The net contributors (Germany, the Netherlands, Sweden, Austria, Finland and Denmark) want deeper cuts to limit what they pay in. The net beneficiaries in central and southern Europe want more money. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said the plan was no basis for agreement because the total was still too high, and ruled out any new joint EU borrowing. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said the sides are "light years away" from a solution. Leaders will try again at the December 17–18 summit. 🔴 @DDGeopolitics

🇹🇷 🇮🇱 🇬🇪 Georgian police tear-gas Beşiktaş fans over Palestine flag, Europa League match halted Beşiktaş's Europa League game against Israel's Hapoel Be'er Sheva descended into chaos in Batumi, Georgia. UEFA had moved the match out of Istanbul to a neutral venue on security grounds. Before kickoff, the Beşiktaş players refused to shake hands with the Israeli team. In the stands, Turkish fans raised a Palestinian flag and a banner reading "If you cannot prevent injustice, make it known to everyone." Georgian police moved in to remove the flag and clashes broke out. Police used batons, tear gas and pepper spray on the Beşiktaş section. One fan was beaten so badly he was left bleeding heavily and taken to hospital. The match was stopped around the 25th minute and the players left the pitch. Clashes continued outside the stadium. Play resumed at 0–0 after a stoppage of more than 45 minutes. Beşiktaş accused Georgian police of using "disproportionate force" against its supporters, and rival club Galatasaray also condemned the crackdown. 🔴 @DDGeopolitics

🇺🇸 🇮🇱 TRIPP corridor advances in Armenia, but US-Israeli strikes on Iran could put it at risk The Armenian government has approved a shareholder agreement establishing the TRIPP Development Company, advancing the US-backed transport corridor in the South Caucasus. The joint Armenian-American venture will oversee the corridor, with the US holding a 74% stake and Armenia 26%. Three of its five board members will be appointed by Washington and two by Yerevan. The corridor is designed to connect Azerbaijan with its Nakhchivan exclave through Armenian territory, running along the Armenian-Iranian border. The Armenian-American company will receive exclusive rights to use designated land and develop infrastructure for 49 years, with an option to extend the arrangement by another 50. 🤔 Iran’s concerns The terms have raised concerns in Iran. TRIPP overlaps with an Iranian-backed route through Armenia to the Black Sea, while any US military presence along the Armenian-Iranian border would pose a direct security threat to Tehran. The timing is also significant: the Trump administration is advancing the project while pursuing a campaign of economic strangulation against Iran on land and at sea. Meanwhile, Western think tanks describe TRIPP as a vital part of the wider Middle Corridor, designed to carry Central Asian energy resources to Europe while bypassing Russia and Iran. The US and Europe are seeking full control over the route. 🔨 Preparatory work underway On November 23, the US, Azerbaijan and Armenia announced the start of the project’s «practical phase.» Plans include roads, railways, oil and gas infrastructure, and power lines, with the route eventually connecting to Turkey’s transport network. The US and Israeli war against Iran, followed by Tehran’s forceful retaliation, had already delayed TRIPP by several months, and the new corridor remains vulnerable. If US military actions against Iran continue, elements of the project could become legitimate Iranian targets, some observers say. 👍 Substack | Chat | @geopolitics_prime
